reforms.description: The Canadian government has developed an innovation strategy aimed at enhancing the national innovation agenda, which includes the provision of the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Investment Tax Credit to encourage private sector R&D. Additionally, the government is examining the efficiency of the SR&ED tax credits to better target R&D in new firms and create more economically efficient framework conditions for enterprises.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reforms aim to enhance the business environment for innovation and support R&D activities, which are expected to raise productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The innovation strategy was developed and the SR&ED tax credit is currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The development of a national innovation strategy and the implementation of significant tax credits represent major structural changes in the innovation policy landscape.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government provides the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Investment Tax Credit, which has the objective of encouraging the private sector to undertake scientific research and experimental development in Canada.

reforms.description: The federal government is encouraged to design a 'Made-in-Canada' climate change programme that achieves greenhouse gas emissions reductions at the lowest economic cost, potentially involving innovation in clean technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The programme aims to foster innovation in clean technologies, which can lead to economic benefits and environmental improvements.
reforms.status_evidence: The government is encouraged to design the programme, indicating it has not yet been implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The proposal for a climate change programme represents a significant but narrower reform focused on sectoral R&D.
reforms.source_quote: Another task will be for the federal government to design its 'Made-in-Canada' climate change programme so that as-yet undefined reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are achieved at the lowest possible economic cost.

reforms.description: The establishment of a business-led Commercialization Partnership Board was recommended to ensure the private sector has a strong voice in public policy design for commercialization.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By ensuring private sector involvement in commercialization policy, the initiative aims to enhance the effectiveness of knowledge transfer and commercialization efforts.
reforms.status_evidence: The recommendation has been acted upon, leading to the establishment of the board.
reforms.importance_rationale: The recommendation for a Commercialization Partnership Board represents a significant step towards improving knowledge transfer mechanisms.
reforms.source_quote: The panel recommended the establishment of a business-led Commercialization Partnership Board to advise the Minister of Industry and ensure the private sector has a strong voice in the design of public policies to improve commercialisation.

reforms.description: A new Canada Commercialization Fellowships Program was proposed to spur private sector hiring of highly qualified personnel with commercialization talents.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By enhancing the talent pool in the private sector, the program aims to improve commercialization efforts and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The program has been proposed but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The proposal for a fellowships program represents a significant initiative to enhance human capital for innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Talent: develop a new Canada Commercialization Fellowships Program; spur private sector hiring of highly qualified personnel with commercialisation talents.

reforms.description: The Canadian authorities announced the Paperwork Burden Reduction Initiative (PBRI), aimed at reducing the costs of paperwork and regulatory compliance for small businesses, facilitating their operations.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By reducing regulatory burdens, the initiative aims to enhance the operational efficiency of small businesses, thereby supporting innovation and growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiative has been announced and is currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant effort to improve the business environment for startups and small enterprises.
reforms.source_quote: In 2005 the Canadian authorities announced the Paperwork Burden Reduction Initiative (PBRI), a public–private sector partnership aimed at reducing the costs of paperwork and regulatory compliance for small businesses.

reforms.description: The Employment Tax Credit, announced in the 2006 federal Budget, aims to offset the tax payable on up to CAD1000 of an individual’s employment income per year, thereby increasing work incentives for low-income workers.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By increasing work incentives for low-income workers, the initiative aims to enhance labor market participation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The Employment Tax Credit was announced and is currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The tax credit represents a significant but narrower reform aimed at improving human capital and labor market outcomes.
reforms.source_quote: The Employment Tax Credit, announced in the 2006 federal Budget, will offset the tax payable on up to CAD1000 of an individual’s employment income per year.

reforms.description: The Workplace Skills Initiative, introduced in the 2004 federal Budget, supports pilot projects aimed at developing skills and literacy in the workplace, particularly for low-wage earners.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By developing skills and literacy, the initiative aims to enhance the employability and productivity of low-wage earners.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiative was introduced and is currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant effort to improve human capital development in the workforce.
reforms.source_quote: Efforts have already been made in this direction in Canada through the Workplace Skills Initiative, introduced in the 2004 federal Budget.
